claims.text: Raymond James offers financial advisors multiple affiliation options it calls AdvisorChoice®, spanning direct employee and independent contractor affiliation as well as third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services division, and its management has said the mix of recruiting across these channels has shifted over time.
In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James states it offers multiple affiliation options, which it refers to as AdvisorChoice®.

In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James states financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James says employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff and serve predominantly retail clients.

On its affiliation-options web page (page content as of April 21, 2026), Raymond James describes its AdvisorChoice options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA.

In its June 2025 investor-day deck, Raymond James describes its affiliation spectrum as spanning Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, noting that the movement to independence is not channel-specific.

In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James says independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for their direct costs and receive a higher payout percentage than employee financial advisors, and may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.

In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James says its domestic RCS division offers third-party RIAs and broker-dealers custodial services, trade execution, research and other support, and that financial advisors associated with RCS firms are not included in Raymond James's advisor counts.

On its 2026 second-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said it is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, offering all the affiliation options and therefore the largest addressable market in the industry.

On its 2025 fourth-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said it has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options—employee, independent contractor, and RIA custody—with critical mass and decades of experience in each, and that it is not a new venture for the firm.

On the 2024 third-quarter earnings call, CEO Paul Reilly said RCS has by far the highest percentage growth, while that year the employee channel led the way, and he expected some improvement in the independent contractor model.

On its 2025 second-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher, while still seeing success in the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA option.

On its 2025 fourth-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said recruiting activity is broad-based across affiliation options but has been more heavily tilted toward the independent contractor side in the last six months.

On its 2026 first-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said it is seeing a good uptick in the employee affiliation option and described the mix shift as relating to the comp ratio because of the payout difference between the independent and employee channels.

On its 2026 second-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said the affiliation options differ in how advisors spend their time day-to-day: the employee option suits those focused on building their books of business, while others want to run a business including building a team, paying benefits, and dealing with real estate and legal aspects.

Trade press reported on October 29, 2026 that Raymond James's recruiting success is spread across all its affiliation channels, with the independent contractor channel seeing the most interest in dollar volume while the RIA custody division is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base.

On its 2026 second-quarter earnings call, Raymond James stated it has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an advisor could want, and it is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates, wanting advisors to fall in love with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James describes its multiple affiliation options collectively as AdvisorChoice, offered to financial advisors who primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RCS division.

On its affiliation-options web page (page content as of April 21, 2026), Raymond James says through AdvisorChoice advisors can match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

On its 2025 first- and third-quarter earnings calls, Raymond James described its best-of-both-worlds value proposition as a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, which it says resonates with advisors across all its affiliation options.

In its June 2025 investor-day deck, Raymond James lists its value proposition pillars as a service-first culture, respect for financial advisor independence, and a comprehensive and growing product and solution set.

On its 2026 second-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said its affiliation strategy lets advisors not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering an advisor- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions.

In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James says its independent contractor advisor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of its support as they determine they need.

In its June 2025 investor-day deck, Raymond James describes its mission for the affiliation models as to inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals, tied to multiple affiliation options, best of both worlds, advisor and book ownership, and RJF stability.

In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James states it competes directly with national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and faces competition from newer entrants including fintechs, as well as indirect competition for investment assets from insurance companies, real estate firms and hedge funds.

In its 2025 10-K, Raymond James says the continued industry-wide trend of financial advisors departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or join existing third-party RIAs some of which are backed by private equity investors, has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.

On its 2025 second-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said it still sees pressure on the existing advisor base from private equity roll-ups, which in the absence of a value proposition compete with big checks.
On its 2025 fourth-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.

On its 2026 second-quarter earnings call, Raymond James said competitors that lack a true differentiated value proposition lead with the highest check.

Raymond James reported $186 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its RIA & Custody Services (RCS) affiliation model as of March 31, 2025.
Raymond James reported AUA associated with firms in its RCS division totaled $217.3 billion as of September 30, 2025.
Raymond James reported PCG AUA associated with RCS firms of $224.6 billion as of December 31, 2025.
Raymond James reported PCG AUA associated with RCS firms of $228.2 billion as of March 31, 2026.
Raymond James reported PCG AUA associated with RCS firms of $251.3 billion as of June 30, 2026.

On its 2026 first-quarter earnings call, Paul Shoukry stated that over the last year much more of Raymond James's recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side, indicating a mix shift toward independent.

On the 2024 third-quarter earnings call, Paul Reilly stated that RCS is by far the highest percentage growth, and in total dollars the employee channel led the way this fiscal year (2024), whereas a couple of years ago it was the independent channel.

The mix has shifted, and this comparison is valid only as management's qualitative statements across periods—independent led a couple of years ago, employee led fiscal 2024, and independent-side recruiting led over the last year, with RCS the highest percentage growth—not as a single quantitative series, since the underlying figures cover different bases and periods.
